newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian deputy premier sacked for city comforts.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian deputy premier sacked for city comforts.

text.p: Ethiopia's parliament on Thursday sacked deputy prime minister and defence minister Tamirat Layne who was accused of "falling prey to the corrupting comfort of city life", the state-run Ethiopian News Agency (ENA) said.
ENA said Prime Minister Meles Zenawi requested parliament to convene an extraordinary session to dismiss Tamirat.

"We are very sorry that Tamirat, who gallantly fought against dictatorship during the armed struggle, has fallen prey to the corrupting comfort of city life," Meles was quoted as telling parliament. He gave no details of the accusations.
State television showed Tamirat, visibly shaken, admitting his mistakes. He requested the parliament to confirm his dismissal.
ENA said parliament approved the appointment in his place of Tefera Walewa, who was nominated by Zenawi.

The Amhara National Democratic Movement (ANDM), a coalition partner of the ruling Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), said in a statement that Tamirat had behaved contrary to the discipline of his party and no longer represented ANDM in any capacity.
ANDM gave no further details of the disciplinary breaches.
